open_questions.question: Does the FULL-SPECTRAL electron sea (many-band tight-binding on L=128, not the mean-field single-field reduction used here) recover the paper's EXACT collapse time t* ~ 5936 t0 at beta=0.001, rather than the ~2650 t0 our reduced model gives?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The mechanism, trends, and order of magnitude are reproduced, but the absolute t* is a factor ~2 low because the itinerant Fermi sea is reduced to one spin-coherent field. The exact t* is set by the true electron-spin backreaction magnitude, which only the full spectral propagation fixes. This is the difference between 'dynamic collapse reproduced' (done) and 'exact t* reproduced'.
open_questions.next_step: Replace the single-field electron with a filled-band ensemble (propagate O(ne*L^2) occupied Bloch states, or a stochastic-trace estimator of s_i = Tr[rho sigma]), keep the same Strang splitter, run on L=128, and compare t* directly to 5936/1748/1236 t0.

open_questions.question: Is the topological transition Q:-1->0 correlated with the nucleation of an intense electron b-field vortex of OPPOSITE charge (Qelec=+1) at the skyrmion core, giving Qfinal = Qsky + Qelec = -1 + 1 = 0 (paper Sec. III, Fig. 4)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the paper's proposed MICROSCOPIC mechanism for the topological change. Our solver already computes the self-consistent electron spin field s(r,t) (it is the torque source), so the b-field b = n.(dx n x dy n) with n=s/|s| is one step away. Confirming the anti-correlation would validate the charge-transfer picture, not just the net Q collapse.
open_questions.next_step: Compute Q_b(t) = Berg-Luscher charge of the electron field n=s/|s| each step; test whether a localized Q_b=+1 structure appears at the core exactly as Q_S climbs from -1 toward 0; render the Fig. 4 snapshots.

open_questions.question: Does the exact self-similar PROFILE f(X) (Eqs. 18-25, expressed via Meijer-G functions) match the rescaled collapsing core from the numerical run, beyond the already-verified exponents (alpha=1, beta=1/2) and the sqrt shrink law?
open_questions.why_it_matters: We verified the EXPONENTS (dimensional balance) and the size law lambda(t)=lambda0/sqrt(1+(s t)^2). The stronger claim is a full data collapse: cores at different times, rescaled by X=r/(t*-t)^{1/2}, fall on one master profile f(X). That tests the self-similar SOLUTION, not just its scaling.
open_questions.next_step: Solve the self-similar ODE Eq. 20-22 for F(X) (or evaluate the Meijer-G form); extract rescaled core profiles from the coupled run near t* and overlay to test the collapse onto f(X)=e^{i phi} F(X).

open_questions.question: How does the exact quantitative shape of the Q(t) curve depend on exchange dissipation beta (the full Fig. 3 family), including the smoothing/sharpening of the transition, not just the monotonic t*(beta) trend we reproduced?
open_questions.why_it_matters: We reproduced t* DECREASING with beta (2653/2523/820 vs paper 5936/1748/1236). The paper further claims dissipation SMOOTHS the transition and lets Q take non-integer values continuously. Reproducing the full Q(t) curve shape across a fine beta scan tests the dissipation physics quantitatively.
open_questions.next_step: Run a denser beta scan (e.g. 0.001-0.2, ~8 points) at L=128 full-spectral, record full Q(t), and overlay against the three-panel Fig. 3; quantify transition width vs beta.

open_questions.question: Where in (lambda0, Bp, ne, a) parameter space does the finite-time singular collapse survive versus becoming a dissipation-smoothed crossover, and does beta=1/2 hold across that region?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper argues the collapse is a genuine finite-time singularity in the continuum dissipationless limit. Mapping the phase boundary (singular collapse vs smooth crossover) and checking the beta=1/2 scaling across it is the deliverable that establishes the singularity's robustness and its dependence on the initial condition and current strength.
open_questions.next_step: Grid (lambda0, Bp, ne) at fixed a, run the coupled solver at each point, fit t* and the shrink exponent, and map the boundary; embarrassingly parallel -> fan out to ALCF Crux or subagents.
